notes: Owner-decided acceptance gates (spec §33.5). Versioned so the thresholds live in one place instead of scattered literals across graders. Precision-first: we would rather ship narrow and correct than broad and wrong. These are the bar for calling a capability design-partner ready; the eval report evaluates each run against them and emits PASS/FAIL per capability. A capability that does not clear every criterion is NOT ready, regardless of how green the rest of the suite looks. Two capability shapes exist: 'fettler-impact' (untagged, kept for back-compat) scores precision/recall on flag_files scenarios; 'regauge-family' scores a migration-recipe family on three behaviours (apply on in-scope repos, refuse on partial-migration repos, abstain on out-of-scope repos) plus open-P0. Recipe families are graded per-scenario pass/fail, so the family thresholds are pass RATES over that family's scenarios; the scenario set is small and hand/procedurally authored, so a single failure fails the gate (that is the intended precision-first behaviour, not an accident of small n).

fettler-impact-analysis.description: Fettler impact analysis: given a structured API change, flag exactly the impacted source files (precision/recall on flag_files scenarios; abstain/no_op scenarios are graded elsewhere).

fettler-abstention.description: Fettler restraint: on an ambiguous rename (>=2 plausible successors) or an already-migrated repo, the correct output is NO confident finding. A distinct capability from impact analysis (which is scored on flag_files recall/precision); this is the precision-first 'do not guess' guard, pooled over the abstain + no_op Fettler scenarios the impact gate excludes.
fettler-abstention.notes: abstention_correctness_min=1.0: a single confident finding on an ambiguous or already-migrated repo is an unsafe automated action (it applies a rename a human never approved), so precision-first admits no partial credit. max_open_p0=0: acting where abstention was required is a P0. This gate has real measured signal today (4 abstain + 2 no_op scenarios in the current suite) and passes; it is included so a future regression that makes the product act on ambiguity fails the gate immediately. It is deliberately separate from fettler-impact-analysis so restraint cannot be traded off against recall.

regauge-runtime-migration.description: ReGauge runtime family (node-runtime-18-to-20, node-runtime-20-to-22). The reference standard: this family already detects residual runtime pins (a CI Dockerfile or extra .nvmrc left on the old major), so it is expected to clear its gate. It is gated anyway as a positive control — a family that always passes proves the gate can distinguish a ready family from an unready one.
regauge-runtime-migration.notes: apply_correctness_min=1.0: a shipped recipe must correctly recognize and (would) apply on every in-scope repo; precision-first admits no partial credit for a config-only bump. refusal_correctness_min=1.0: every partial-migration repo (residual pin outside allowedPaths) must return status=incomplete; a single false 'applicable' ships a divergent runtime. abstention_correctness_min=1.0: an already-migrated or unsupported-major repo must not match. max_open_p0=0: no confidently-wrong application. Thresholds are pass rates over this family's scenarios.

regauge-sdk-migration.description: ReGauge SDK family (aws-sdk-js-v2-to-v3, stripe-node-v10-to-v11, googleapis-v25-to-v26). These recipes swap or bump a dependency repo-wide while editing only their two allowlisted source files, and their verifiers check only those files. The residual scenarios prove that a third consumer left on the old surface must force a refusal, not a signed evidence record for a repo that no longer installs.
regauge-sdk-migration.notes: Same precision-first rationale as the runtime family. refusal_correctness_min=1.0 is the load-bearing gate here: until residual detection covers the SDK precondition kinds (a fix landing in packages/transformer/src/recipe.ts), the residual scenarios report status=applicable and this criterion fails at 0.0 — the correct, honest signal, not a threshold to tune away. Thresholds are pass rates over this family's scenarios.

regauge-framework-migration.description: ReGauge framework family (react-dom-17-to-18). Migrates render/hydrate call sites in the allowlisted entrypoints; a residual entrypoint still calling the legacy ReactDOM.render outside allowedPaths must force a refusal.
regauge-framework-migration.notes: Same precision-first rationale. Whether the residual criterion passes depends on residual detection reaching the react precondition kind in recipe.ts; reported honestly per run. Thresholds are pass rates over this family's scenarios.

regauge-internal-api-migration.description: ReGauge internal-API family (internal-api-acme-user-rename and the registry rename recipes). Renames an exported symbol across allowlisted consumers; a residual consumer outside allowedPaths still calling the old name must force a refusal.
regauge-internal-api-migration.notes: Same precision-first rationale. Whether the residual criterion passes depends on residual detection reaching the internal_api precondition kinds in recipe.ts; reported honestly per run. Thresholds are pass rates over this family's scenarios.

not_measured.notes: Capabilities the product HAS but the current eval substrate cannot score. Recorded here (not silently omitted) so gate coverage is honest: a capability is either gated on a real measured dimension above, or listed here with the experiment that would make it measurable. NONE of these is gated on an invented threshold. This list is the Phase 2 backlog: each entry names the smallest change that would move it into 'capabilities'. Ownership tags (Claude/Codex/Shared) follow the Phase 0 blocker assignment.

capabilities.reason: Both runners are analyze-only (evals/runners/regauge-runner.ts calls analyzeRecipe and stops; fettler-runner.ts sets useLlm:false and calls analyzeImpact only). Nothing applies a recipe, installs dependencies, compiles, or runs the subject repo's tests, so 'the migration is complete and the repo still installs/compiles' is unobservable. The gated ReGauge families measure the analyze DECISION (refuse vs apply), not a verified applied result.
capabilities.experiment: An apply-and-verify harness that runs applyRecipe/executeRecipeInWorkspace in a fenced sandbox, installs and builds the migrated tree, and grades an independent fail-to-pass/pass-to-pass judge. Gate on post-apply verification pass rate. (Phase 2 blocker #5, Claude.)

capabilities.reason: The Fettler runner exercises impact analysis only; migration-patch generation, the agentic repair loop, and GitHub PR delivery are not invoked (they need a seeded DB, a sandbox, and GitHub credentials). Recorded per run as unmeasured_dimensions, never scored.
capabilities.experiment: A seeded-DB + sandbox + delivery integration harness that drives the generation/repair/delivery lane on a synthetic repo and grades patch correctness and delivery honesty. Gate on generated-patch correctness once it exists.

capabilities.reason: Both runners run the deterministic path with the model off (useLlm:false / analyzeRecipe), so model, provider, tokens, and cost are genuinely null (no model was called) rather than measured. There is no routing decision to score because no model path runs.
capabilities.experiment: A live-model eval lane (the one .github/workflows/regauge-production.yml already runs) feeding routing decisions, token counts, and measured cost into the run record. Gate on cost-per-outcome and routing-decision quality once a second executor is genuinely eligible.

capabilities.reason: recall@k for the retrieval layer has a numerator on at most one path and no denominator anywhere; the harness cannot see which files the model was shown, so 'the required file was never retrieved' is undiagnosable. Fine-tuning to compensate for a retrieval defect is the failure mode spec 17.4 warns against, so this must be measured before any training targets it.
capabilities.experiment: A retrieval benchmark that records the candidate set the product examined and scores it against the ground-truth impacted files (recall@k with a real denominator). (Phase 2 blocker #10, Claude.)

capabilities.reason: gl_edges.confidence is assigned by fiat at write time and never validated against an outcome; there is no graph-completeness measure and no graph-gated decision in production. The harness scores product findings, not the graph the findings came from.
capabilities.experiment: Wire the already-written, zero-caller runImpactBenchmark and evaluateConfidenceCalibration (packages/graph-learn) into a scored eval so a confidence:0.7 edge can be checked to be right ~70% of the time. Gate on calibration error once it reports.

capabilities.reason: In deployed config, production verification refuses with exit 126 for essentially every real repo command, and a refusal is indistinguishable downstream from a genuine test failure; the sandbox backend that ran is recorded nowhere. The analyze-only harness never reaches verification, so 'verified' cannot be validated as a trustworthy label here.
capabilities.experiment: Capture per-check exit codes and the sandbox backend that actually ran, and grade a refusal distinctly from a failure. Gate on verifier-refusal rate and backend provenance once captured. (Phase 2 blocker #7, Shared.)

capabilities.reason: completes_within_budget IS measured (the huge-monorepo scenario runs under a hard 120s budget and records a SCALE_FAILURE if it blows it), but n=1: there is exactly one large-repo data point. Gating latency on a single scenario would require inventing a budget threshold that one run cannot justify, so it is measured-but-not-gated rather than gated on a fabricated number.
capabilities.experiment: A scale ladder (several repo sizes across the file-count axis in AnalysisActivity.filesExamined) that plots latency against repo size; set a budget threshold from the measured curve. Gate on p95 latency at a defined repo size.
